chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Uthman ibn Isa and Harun ibn Kharjah, who said: 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying.'
Have mercy on me from what there is no strength for me with, nor any patience for me upon.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (a title for Imam Al-Sadiq)

ai.seo_question: What is a short supplication for when one lacks strength or patience?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi through the chain of Uthman ibn Isa and Harun ibn Kharaja, this supplication encapsulates the Shia theological emphasis on *istidafa* (seeking capacity) alongside *istighatha* (seeking help), acknowledging that human endurance is finite. It serves as a concise liturgical tool for believers to invoke divine mercy specifically for burdens that exceed their natural *taqa* (capacity) and *sabr* (patience), reinforcing the balance between human effort and reliance on God's grace.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin saeed, from Usman Bin Isa and Haroun Bin Kharjat who said, 
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying:
‘Have Mercy on me<sup>asws</sup> from what there is no strength for me with I, nor any patience for me<sup>asws</sup> upon it’.
en.sarwar: 22. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al- Husayn ibn Sa’id from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa and Harun ibn Kharijah who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘
(O Allah) grant mercy upon me in the matters for which I do not have the ability to remain patient.’”
